Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://docs.btcd.fi/token-overviews/sbtcd.md). # sBTCD sBTCD is the yield-bearing staked version of BTCD. Holding sBTCD entitles the holder to a pro-rata share of the yield generated by the BTCD Portfolio in excess of what is required to maintain the peg. ### Mechanics * Stake: deposit BTCD into the staking contract; receive sBTCD. * Appreciation: yield earned by the portfolio is paid into the staking contract on a periodic basis. This causes 1 sBTCD to represent a progressively larger amount of BTCD over time. * Unstake: redeem sBTCD for the underlying BTCD. ### Yield smoothing Rather than distributing yield exactly as it is earned, payouts reflect a moving average of recent earnings governed by a smoothing factor. This serves two purposes: * Smoother, more predictable yield for stakers. * A natural overcollateralization buffer, since yield is distributed with a lag to what is earned. *The exact smoothing factor and payout cadence may be adjusted over time*. ### Yield concentration Every asset in the BTCD Portfolio earns yield, regardless of whether the corresponding BTCD is staked. But only stakers receive yield distributions. As a result, sBTCD holders earn yield not only on their own capital but also on capital held by unstaked BTCD holders. This concentrates the portfolio's yield into a smaller staked supply, potentially making sBTCD's yield meaningfully higher than the underlying assets' average yield. ### The BTCD/sBTCD DeFi Dynamic The BTCD/sBTCD pair creates a self-reinforcing demand cycle, analogous to the USDe/sUSDe loop: * Users deposit sBTCD as collateral and borrow BTCD against it. * Borrowed BTCD is swapped for more sBTCD, which is added as additional collateral. This is the "loop." * Borrowing demand for BTCD creates lending yield for users who supply BTCD to lending markets. * The result: BTCD earns yield even when unstaked, while sBTCD remains the primary yield-bearing instrument. This dynamic is structurally beneficial: the more BTCD remains unstaked, the more yield concentrates in sBTCD, increasing sBTCD's yield, which increases looping demand, which increases BTCD lending yield.
\

# BTCD

BTCD is the base token of the Bitcoin Dollar protocol. It tracks a peg defined as continuous 50/50 BTC/USD exposure.

### Mechanics

* Mint: users deposit USDC into the protocol and receive BTCD at the current peg price.
* Redeem: users return BTCD to the protocol and receive USDC at the current peg price. Redemption is instant.
* Volatility: BTCD's USD-denominated volatility is approximately half of BTC's, by virtue of its 50/50 construction.

### Use cases

* Holders who want exposure to the BTC trend without full BTC volatility.
* Lending: BTCD is mechanically well-suited as lending collateral because of its instant redeemability.
* AMM liquidity: BTCD paired with WBTC or USDC offer yield bearing 75% or 25% BTC exposure respectively.
* Options margin and instant-exit products.

devdoc.details: This contract implements:      - ERC4626 tokenized vault standard for BTCD staking      - Linear vesting of rewards over configurable periods      - Optional cooldown mechanism for withdrawals via silo contract      - Two-tier blacklist system (soft and full restrictions)      - Administrative functions for emergency token rescue and redistribution      - ERC20Permit for gasless approvals

name().details: Returns the name of the token.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

decimals().details: Resolves ambiguity between ERC20 and ERC4626 decimals declarations

returns._0: Always returns 18 decimals

params._name: ERC20 name for the staking shares token
params._asset: The underlying ERC20 token to be staked (BTCD)
params._owner: Address that will have DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (contract owner)
params._symbol: ERC20 symbol for the staking shares token

constructor.details: Sets up:      - Creates new Silo contract for cooldown escrow      - Sets initial cooldown duration to 7 days      - Sets initial vesting period to 8 hours      - Grants roles to provided addresses

totalAssets().details: Overrides ERC4626 totalAssets to exclude unvested rewards from share price calculations      This ensures that unvested rewards don't dilute existing shareholders until they vest

returns._0: The total assets in the vault minus any unvested reward amounts

nonces(address).details: Returns the current nonce for `owner`. This value must be included whenever a signature is generated for {permit}. Every successful call to {permit} increases ``owner``'s nonce by one. This prevents a signature from being used multiple times.

params.receiver: The address to send assets to after cooldown expires

unstake(address).details: Can only be called after cooldown period has elapsed or cooldown is disabled      Withdraws user's assets from the silo contract      Resets user's cooldown information      If cooldownDuration becomes 0, allows immediate unstaking regardless of cooldown end time

DOMAIN_SEPARATOR().details: Returns the domain separator used in the encoding of the signature for {permit}, as defined by {EIP712}.

getUnvestedAmount().details: Calculates based on time elapsed since last distribution and vesting period      Returns 0 if vesting period has fully elapsed

returns._0: The amount of rewards that are still linearly vesting

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

mint(uint256,address).details: See {IERC4626-mint}. As opposed to {deposit}, minting is allowed even if the vault is in a state where the price of a share is zero. In this case, the shares will be minted without requiring any assets to be deposited.

params.assets: The amount of assets to initiate cooldown for

cooldownAssets(uint256).details: Only works when cooldownDuration > 0 (cooldown enabled)      Burns shares and transfers assets to silo contract      Updates user's cooldown information      User must call unstake() after cooldown period expires

returns.shares: The number of shares being redeemed

params.shares: The number of shares to initiate cooldown for

cooldownShares(uint256).details: Only works when cooldownDuration > 0 (cooldown enabled)      Burns shares and transfers assets to silo contract      Updates user's cooldown information      User must call unstake() after cooldown period expires

returns.assets: The amount of assets being redeemed

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `amount` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `amount`.

params.amount: The amount of rewards to distribute over the vesting period

transferInRewards(uint256).details: Only callable by REWARD_DISTRIBUTOR_ROLE      Cannot be called while previous rewards are still vesting      Amount must be greater than zero      Transfers tokens from caller to this contract

params.duration: Duration of the cooldown (0 = instant withdrawal, max 90 days)

setCooldownDuration(uint24).details: Only callable by DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE      When set to 0, enables instant withdrawals/redemptions      When non-zero, requires users to use cooldown functions

updateVestingPeriod(uint24).details: Only callable by DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE      Cannot be updated while rewards are still vesting      Must be greater than 0 and not exceed MAX_VESTING_PERIOD

params.isFullBlacklisting: true for full restriction (all operations blocked), false for soft restriction (deposits only)

addToBlacklist(address,bool).details: Only callable by BLACKLIST_MANAGER_ROLE      Cannot blacklist the contract owner      Soft restrictions: prevents deposits/minting only      Full restrictions: prevents all operations and transfers

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Overrides AccessControl renounceRole to always revert      This prevents accidental or malicious role renunciation

devdoc.details: Architecture ================   BTCD <-> MintingProxy <-> [BTCDMinting, VaultMinting]   USDC is accepted externally and converted to sUSDS internally via   LitePSM (USDC<>USDS) + ERC-4626 (USDS<>sUSDS) so the contract earns   yield on USD liquidity. On burns/withdrawals, sUSDS is redeemed back   to USDC for the caller. Role Separation (Principle of Least Privilege) ==============================================   Owner              — Configuration and fund management: limits, oracles, proxy,                        whitelist, pause, role assignment. Can withdraw collateral to                        whitelisted addresses.   Fee Updater        — The only address that can change mint/burn fees.   Anyone (mint/burn) — Can call mint/burn, but the `to` recipient must be whitelisted.   Collateral Manager — Engine integration: sweep USDC, transfer custody, multicall. Per-Block Capacity Limits ========================= Following BTCDMinting's pattern: maxMintPerBlock / maxRedeemPerBlock. Accumulators reset each block (tracked by block.number). This prevents flash-loan-scale minting within a single block. Pricing Model ============= The BTCD/USD price is read from a single owner-settable Chainlink-conform feed (btcdOracle). The BTCD price model lives in the feed, not in this contract. Oracle Architecture ===================   btcdOracle — BTCD/USD Chainlink-conform feed (latestRoundData/decimals),                validated via ChainlinkAdapter with an owner-set staleness                bound; a zero or invalid answer reverts, so mint/burn halts                instead of mispricing.   WBTC/USD   — composed from two owner-set Chainlink feeds:                WBTC/BTC (~24h heartbeat, captures WBTC depeg) multiplied by                BTC/USD (~1h heartbeat), each with its own staleness bound.                No direct WBTC/USD Chainlink feed exists on mainnet. sUSDS pricing uses the on-chain ERC-4626 exchange rate (convertToAssets) since the contract redeems through the vault directly — the canonical rate is the actual price received, making an external oracle unnecessary and less accurate.

devdoc.details: Architecture ================   BTCD <-> MintingProxy <-> [BTCDMinting, VaultMinting]   USDC is accepted externally and converted to sUSDS internally via   LitePSM (USDC<>USDS) + ERC-4626 (USDS<>sUSDS) so the contract earns   yield on USD liquidity. On burns/withdrawals, sUSDS is redeemed back   to USDC for the caller. Role Separation (Principle of Least Privilege) ==============================================   Owner              — Configuration and fund management: limits, oracles, proxy,                        whitelist, pause, role assignment. Can withdraw collateral to                        whitelisted addresses.   Fee Updater        — The only address that can change mint/burn fees.   Anyone (mint/burn) — Can call mint/burn, but the `to` recipient must be whitelisted.   Collateral Manager — Engine integration: sweep USDC, transfer custody, multicall. Per-Block Capacity Limits ========================= Following BTCDMinting's pattern: maxMintPerBlock / maxRedeemPerBlock. Accumulators reset each block (tracked by block.number). This prevents flash-loan-scale minting within a single block. Pricing Model ============= The BTCD/USD price is read from a single owner-settable Chainlink-conform feed (btcdOracle). The BTCD price model lives in the feed, not in this contract. Oracle Architecture ===================   btcdOracle — BTCD/USD Chainlink-conform feed (latestRoundData/decimals),                validated via ChainlinkAdapter with an owner-set staleness                bound; a zero or invalid answer reverts, so mint/burn halts                instead of mispricing.   WBTC/USD   — composed from two owner-set Chainlink feeds:                WBTC/BTC (~24h heartbeat, captures WBTC depeg) multiplied by                BTC/USD (~1h heartbeat), each with its own staleness bound.                No direct WBTC/USD Chainlink feed exists on mainnet. sUSDS pricing uses the on-chain ERC-4626 exchange rate (convertToAssets) since the contract redeems through the vault directly — the canonical rate is the actual price received, making an external oracle unnecessary and less accurate.

params.limit: Maximum BTCD per block (18 decimals). Zero disables redemptions.

params.addr: Address to whitelist. Must not be zero.

burnUSDC(address,uint256,uint256).details: Burns BTCD from msg.sender, redeems sUSDS to USDC via LitePSM, sends to `to`.

burnWBTC(address,uint256,uint256).details: Burns BTCD from msg.sender, sends WBTC to `to`. Fee applied to BTCD input.

mintUSDC(address,uint256,uint256).details: Pulls USDC from msg.sender, converts to sUSDS internally, mints BTCD to `to`.

mintWBTC(address,uint256,uint256).details: Pulls WBTC from msg.sender, mints BTCD to `to`. Fee applied to input amount.

burn(address,uint256,uint256,uint256).details: Splits redemption across WBTC and sUSDS based on current collateral ratio.      Blended fee: balanced portion at burnBalancedFee, excess at burnOneFee.

mint(address,uint256,uint256,uint256).details: Balanced portion charged mintBalancedFee, excess charged mintOneFee.
